# Memo — AI Vendor Proposal: Invoice Processing and Inquiry Triage

**To:** Andre Pierre-Louis, Chief Operating Officer
**Re:** Go/no-go on the proposed platform
**Recommendation:** Conditional go, invoices first; inquiries only after the pilot clears two conditions below.

## 1. Fit

**Invoice processing fits well.** The work is high-volume (2,900 a month), rule-bound (match to purchase order, post for approval), and the current error rate of 4 percent is already costing $3,100 a month in rework and late fees. Invoice reading is the vendor's mature product; the reference customers' 55 to 65 percent time savings are for this use case.

**Inquiry triage fits partially.** Classifying 9,400 inquiries by topic and urgency is well suited to the platform. Drafting replies is not, for two reasons in the appendix. Fourteen percent of inquiries are maintenance emergencies or legal notices, where a wrong or slow machine draft has real consequences. And 9 percent of inquiries are in Haitian Creole, which the classifier was not trained on, so roughly one in eleven messages will be misrouted or unread by the model. Triage is the weaker use case, and reply drafting should be out of scope for the pilot.

## 2. Return and payback

**Invoices.** 3.5 staff at $58,000 is $203,000 a year. The vendor promises a 70 percent time reduction: $142,100 a year. The reference range of 55 to 65 percent gives $111,650 to $131,950. Add error reduction: if errors fall by half, rework and late fees fall by about $18,600 a year.

**Inquiries.** Six staff at $52,000 is $312,000; 55 percent of that is triage, $171,600. The vendor promises a 60 percent reduction: $102,960. Applying the same discount as the invoice reference range (roughly 0.85 of the promise) gives about $87,500, and the Creole gap means 9 percent of volume gets no benefit, so about $79,600.

**Cost.** $6,500 a month is $78,000 a year, plus $48,000 implementation in year one.

**Vendor scenario, both use cases:** savings $142,100 + $18,600 + $102,960 = $263,660 a year against $78,000; net $185,660; payback on the $48,000 implementation in about three months.

**Reference scenario, both use cases:** $111,650 + $18,600 + $79,600 = $209,850; net $131,850; payback in about four and a half months.

**Invoices only, reference scenario:** $130,250 against $78,000; net $52,250; payback in about eleven months.

The result is most sensitive to the invoice time-savings percentage. Each five-point drop below 55 percent removes about $10,000 a year; at 30 percent savings, invoices alone do not cover the subscription.

## 3. Risks and controls

Blocking before signing:
- **Tenant personally identifiable information leaves our systems.** Control: the data-processing agreement must name US storage, prohibit training on our data, and include deletion on termination. Owner: COO with counsel.
- **Machine-drafted replies on emergencies and legal notices.** Control: reply drafting disabled for the emergency and legal categories in the contract, not just the settings. Owner: inquiry team lead.

Managed after signing:
- **Haitian Creole inquiries misclassified.** Control: any message the classifier scores below 70 percent confidence, or detects as a language outside English and Spanish, routes to a human queue; measure Creole misroute rate monthly. Owner: inquiry team lead.
- **Invoice matching errors.** Control: human approval stays on every invoice above $2,000 and on any match below 90 percent confidence; sample 50 auto-posted invoices a week. Owner: accounts-payable supervisor.
- **Model wrong in ways nobody sees.** Control: a monthly reconciliation of model decisions against outcomes (late fees, tenant complaints about routing). Owner: operations analyst.
- **Three-year lock-in.** Control: negotiate a twelve-month exit if pilot thresholds are missed. Owner: COO.

## 4. Rollout plan

**Pilot scope:** invoice processing for the twelve largest associations, about 1,100 invoices a month, plus inquiry classification (no drafting) for two rental communities.

**Duration:** ninety days after implementation.

**Success metrics:** invoice handling time per invoice (target under 5 minutes, from 11); invoice error rate (target under 2 percent); inquiry first-response time in the pilot communities (target under 8 hours, from 19); Creole misroute rate (target under 5 percent).

**Stopping rule:** if invoice time savings are below 40 percent at day 60, stop the rollout and invoke the exit clause. Forty percent is where the invoice case alone falls to about a two-year payback.

## 5. Recommendation

Conditional go. Sign for invoice processing with the two blocking controls in the contract and the twelve-month exit. Run inquiry classification in the pilot without drafting. Expand to inquiries company-wide only if the Creole misroute rate is under 5 percent and first-response time is under 8 hours at day 90. Do not enable reply drafting for emergencies or legal notices under any scenario.

# Memo — Renewal Decision: AI Invoice Matching and Message Triage Platform

**To:** Dana Whitfield, Chief Operating Officer
**Re:** Three-year renewal on the newer release
**Recommendation:** Renew on conditions — invoices only at signature; message handling stays in a bounded trial until two thresholds below are cleared.

## 1. Fit

**Invoice matching fits the work well.** Volume is high (3,400 a month), the steps are rule-bound (match to purchase order, route for approval), and the current 5 percent error rate already costs about $3,600 a month in rework and late fees. Invoice reading is the vendor's mature module, and the 50 to 60 percent savings its reference customers report on the newer release are for this module.

**Message handling fits only partly.** Sorting 11,000 messages a month by topic and urgency suits the platform. Drafting the replies does not, for two reasons in the appendix. Fifteen percent of messages are habitability emergencies or eviction and legal notices, where a wrong or slow machine draft carries real exposure. And 8 percent of messages arrive in Vietnamese, which the classifier was never trained on, so roughly one message in twelve is misrouted or invisible to the model. Message handling is the weaker case; reply drafting should stay out of scope, and year one confirms it — triage time fell 35 percent against a promised 60 percent.

## 2. Return and payback

**Invoices.** Four clerks at $60,000 is $240,000 a year. The vendor's promised 70 percent reduction is $168,000. The reference range of 50 to 60 percent gives $120,000 to $144,000; year one actually delivered 42 percent, so plan on the bottom of that range, $120,000. Add error reduction: if errors fall by half, rework and late fees drop about $21,600 a year.

**Messages.** Seven staff at $54,000 is $378,000; half of that is triage, $189,000. The vendor's promised 60 percent reduction is $113,400. Discounting the promise the way the invoice reference range discounts it (about 0.8) gives roughly $90,700, and because the Vietnamese 8 percent gets no benefit, about $83,400.

**Cost.** $7,200 a month is $86,400 a year, plus the one-time $36,000 upgrade fee in the first renewal year.

**Vendor scenario, both use cases:** $168,000 + $21,600 + $113,400 = $303,000 against $86,400; net $216,600; the $36,000 upgrade fee pays back in about two months.

**Reference scenario, both use cases:** $120,000 + $21,600 + $83,400 = $225,000; net $138,600; payback in about three months.

**Invoices only, reference scenario:** $141,600 against $86,400; net $55,200; payback in about eight months.

The answer turns most on the invoice time-savings percentage. Every five points below 50 percent removes about $12,000 a year; below roughly 27 percent the invoice case alone no longer covers the subscription.

## 3. Risks and controls

Must be fixed before signature:
- **Resident personally identifiable information sits outside our systems.** Control: the data-processing agreement must name US storage, bar training on Harborlight data, and require deletion at termination. Owner: COO with outside counsel.
- **Machine-written replies on emergencies and legal notices.** Control: reply drafting switched off for the emergency and legal categories in the contract itself, not merely in the settings screen. Owner: service desk manager.

Managed after signature:
- **Vietnamese messages misclassified.** Control: any message the classifier scores below 70 percent confidence, or detects as a language other than English or Spanish, drops into a human queue; report the Vietnamese misroute rate monthly. Owner: service desk manager.
- **Invoice matching errors.** Control: keep human approval on every invoice above $2,000 and on any match below 90 percent confidence; audit 50 auto-posted invoices a week. Owner: accounts-payable supervisor.
- **Model wrong with nobody noticing.** Control: monthly reconciliation of model decisions against outcomes — late fees paid, resident complaints about routing. Owner: operations analyst.
- **Three-year lock-in after a year of missed targets.** Control: negotiate a twelve-month exit if the trial thresholds are missed. Owner: COO.

## 4. Rollout plan

**Trial scope:** invoice matching for the fifteen largest associations, about 1,300 invoices a month, plus message classification without drafting for two rental portfolios.

**Duration:** ninety days on a bridge extension, before the three-year term starts.

**Success metrics:** invoice handling time per invoice (target under 7 minutes, from 12); invoice error rate (target under 2.5 percent); first-response time in the trial portfolios (target under 9 hours, from 21); Vietnamese misroute rate (target under 5 percent).

**Stopping rule:** if invoice time savings sit below 35 percent at day 60, do not sign the renewal. Thirty-five percent is the point where invoices alone stretch to roughly a two-year payback on the upgrade fee — and it is below what the tool already achieved in year one, so it is a fair floor.

## 5. Recommendation

Renew on conditions. Sign the invoice module only, with both blocking controls written into the contract and a twelve-month exit. Run message classification inside the ninety-day trial with drafting disabled. Extend message handling across the company only if the Vietnamese misroute rate is under 5 percent and first-response time is under 9 hours at day 90. # Memo — AI Vendor Proposal: Servicing Document Processing and Borrower Inquiry Triage

**To:** Dana Whitfield, VP of Shared Services
**Re:** Go/no-go on the proposed platform
**Recommendation:** Conditional go, documents first; inquiries only after the pilot clears the two conditions below.

## 1. Fit

**Document processing fits well.** The work is high-volume (3,200 items a month), rule-bound (extract the figures, match to the servicing record, post for review), and the current 5 percent posting error rate already costs $3,600 a month in corrections, interest adjustments and reimbursed late charges. Document extraction is the vendor's mature product, and the reference banks' 50 to 60 percent savings are measured on this use case.

**Inquiry triage fits only partly.** Sorting 8,600 borrower messages by topic and urgency suits the platform. Drafting the replies does not, for two reasons visible in the appendix. Twelve percent of inquiries involve delinquency, hardship, collections or bankruptcy, where a wrong or late machine draft creates real regulatory exposure. And 8 percent of inquiries arrive in Vietnamese, a language the classifier never saw, so roughly one message in twelve will be misrouted or missed. Triage is the weaker case, and reply drafting should sit outside the pilot.

## 2. Return and payback

**Documents.** 4 staff at $61,000 is $244,000 a year. The vendor's promised 70 percent reduction is $170,800. The reference range of 50 to 60 percent gives $122,000 to $146,400. Add error reduction: if posting errors fall by half, the $43,200 annual correction cost drops by about $21,600.

**Inquiries.** Five representatives at $54,000 is $270,000; 60 percent of that is triage, $162,000. The vendor's promised 60 percent reduction is $97,200. Applying the same haircut the document reference range implies (about 0.85 of the promise) gives roughly $82,600, and the Vietnamese gap means 8 percent of volume gets no benefit, so about $76,000.

**Cost.** $7,200 a month is $86,400 a year, plus $54,000 implementation in year one.

**Vendor scenario, both use cases:** $170,800 + $21,600 + $97,200 = $289,600 against $86,400; net $203,200; payback on the $54,000 implementation in about three months.

**Reference scenario, both use cases:** $122,000 + $21,600 + $76,000 = $219,600; net $133,200; payback in about five months.

**Documents only, reference scenario:** $143,600 against $86,400; net $57,200; payback in about eleven months.

The result is most sensitive to the document time-savings percentage. Every five-point drop below 50 percent removes roughly $12,200 a year; below about 27 percent savings, the document case alone no longer covers the subscription.

## 3. Risks and controls

Blocking before signature:
- **Borrower nonpublic personal information leaves the bank.** Control: the data-processing agreement must name US hosting, bar training on our data, and require deletion at termination; vendor added to the third-party risk register. Owner: VP of Shared Services with counsel.
- **Machine-generated replies on delinquency, hardship and bankruptcy matters.** Control: reply drafting contractually disabled for those categories, not merely switched off in configuration. Owner: servicing team lead.

Managed after signature:
- **Vietnamese inquiries misclassified.** Control: any message scored below 70 percent confidence, or detected as a language other than English or Spanish, routes to a human queue; misroute rate reported monthly. Owner: servicing team lead.
- **Document extraction and posting errors.** Control: human review stays on every item above $2,000 and on any extraction below 90 percent confidence; 50 auto-posted items sampled weekly. Owner: servicing operations supervisor.
- **Model wrong in ways nobody notices.** Control: monthly reconciliation of model decisions against outcomes — reimbursed late charges, escrow corrections, borrower complaints about routing — under the bank's model risk management standard. Owner: operations analyst.
- **Three-year lock-in.** Control: negotiate a twelve-month exit if the pilot thresholds are missed. Owner: VP of Shared Services.

## 4. Rollout plan

**Pilot scope:** document processing for the consumer and small-business portfolios, about 1,200 items a month, plus inquiry classification only (no drafting) for the mortgage servicing queue.

**Duration:** ninety days after implementation.

**Success metrics:** handling time per document (target under 6 minutes, from 12); posting error rate (target under 2.5 percent); first-response time in the pilot queue (target under 9 hours, from 21); Vietnamese misroute rate (target under 5 percent).

**Stopping rule:** if document time savings are below 35 percent at day 60, halt the rollout and invoke the exit clause. Thirty-five percent is the point where the document case alone stretches to roughly a two-and-a-half-year payback.

## 5. Recommendation

Conditional go. Sign for document processing with both blocking controls written into the contract and the twelve-month exit in place. Run inquiry classification inside the pilot without reply drafting. Extend to inquiries across servicing only if the Vietnamese misroute rate is under 5 percent and first-response time is under 9 hours at day 90. Do not enable reply drafting on delinquency, hardship, collections or bankruptcy messages under any scenario.

**To:** Dana Okonjo, City Manager
**Re:** Board request — justification for proceeding with the signed platform contract
**Recommendation:** Conditional go. Proceed with tendering first; message handling only after the pilot clears the two conditions named below.

## 1. Fit

**Load tendering fits well.** The work is high-volume (3,000 tenders a month), rule-bound (match freight to a qualified carrier at a contracted rate, then tender and confirm), and today's 4 percent error rate already costs about $3,100 a month in re-tendering, missed appointments and late-delivery penalties. **Message triage fits partially.** Classifying 9,200 driver and shipper messages by topic and urgency suits the platform. Drafting replies does not, for two reasons in the appendix. Fourteen percent of messages concern hazardous-materials loads or service-failure claims, where a wrong or slow machine draft has safety and liability consequences. And 9 percent of driver messages are in Punjabi, which the classifier was never trained on, so roughly one message in eleven will be misrouted or left unread by the model. Triage is the weaker use case, and reply drafting should be out of scope for the pilot.

## 2. Return and payback

**Tendering.** 3.5 dispatchers at $58,000 is $203,000 a year. The vendor promises a 70 percent time reduction: $142,100 a year. The reference range of 55 to 65 percent gives $111,650 to $131,950. Add error reduction: if tender errors fall by half, the $3,100 a month ($37,200 a year) falls by about $18,600.

**Messages.** Six customer-desk staff at $52,000 is $312,000; 55 percent of that is triage, $171,600. The vendor promises a 60 percent reduction: $102,960. Applying the same discount the reference customers applied to the tendering promise (roughly 0.85) gives about $87,500, and because the Punjabi gap means 9 percent of volume gets no benefit, about $79,600.

**Cost.** $6,500 a month is $78,000 a year, plus $48,000 implementation in year one.

**Vendor scenario, both use cases:** $142,100 + $18,600 + $102,960 = $263,660 a year against $78,000; net $185,660; payback on the $48,000 implementation in about three months.

**Reference scenario, both use cases:** $111,650 + $18,600 + $79,600 = $209,850; net $131,850; payback in about four and a half months.

**Tendering only, reference scenario:** $130,250 against $78,000; net $52,250; payback in about eleven months.

The result is most sensitive to the tender time-savings percentage. Each five-point drop below 55 percent removes roughly $10,000 a year; at 30 percent savings, tendering alone no longer covers the subscription.

## 3. Risks and controls

Blocking before implementation kickoff:
- **Driver and shipper personal data leaves authority systems.** Control: amend the data-processing agreement to name US storage, prohibit training on our data, and require deletion on termination. Owner: city manager with the city attorney.
- **Machine-drafted replies on hazmat loads and service-failure claims.** Control: reply drafting disabled for those two categories in the contract language, not only in the platform settings. Owner: customer desk supervisor.

Managed after kickoff:
- **Punjabi messages misclassified.** Control: any message the classifier scores below 70 percent confidence, or detects as a language outside English and Spanish, routes to a human queue; report the Punjabi misroute rate monthly. Owner: customer desk supervisor.
- **Tender and carrier-matching errors.** Control: dispatcher approval stays on every tender above $2,000 and on any match below 90 percent confidence; audit 50 auto-tendered loads a week. Owner: dispatch manager.
- **Model wrong in ways nobody sees.** Control: monthly reconciliation of model decisions against outcomes — on-time delivery, detention hours, late-delivery penalties, shipper complaints about routing. Owner: operations analyst.
- **Three-year commitment already signed.** Control: negotiate an amendment before kickoff giving the authority a twelve-month exit if pilot thresholds are missed. Owner: city manager.

## 4. Rollout plan

**Pilot scope:** load tendering for the twelve largest shipper accounts, about 1,100 tenders a month, plus message classification with no drafting for two of those accounts.

**Duration:** ninety days after kickoff.

**Success metrics:** handling time per tender (target under 5 minutes, from 11); tender error rate (target under 2 percent); first-response time on pilot-account messages (target under 8 hours, from 19); Punjabi misroute rate (target under 5 percent).

**Stopping rule:** if tender time savings are below 40 percent at day 60, halt the rollout and invoke the amended exit. Forty percent is the point where the tendering case alone stretches to roughly a two-year payback.

## 5. Recommendation

Conditional go, and the board should be told the conditions are not optional. Proceed with load tendering only after the two blocking controls and the twelve-month exit are in the amended contract. Run message classification in the pilot without drafting. Extend messaging to all accounts only if the Punjabi misroute rate is under 5 percent and first-response time is under 8 hours at day 90. Do not enable reply drafting on hazmat loads or service-failure claims under any scenario.

Applying the same haircut the credentialing range implies (about 0.85 of the promise) gives roughly $87,500, and because the Tagalog volume gets no benefit, about $79,600.

**Cost.** $6,500 a month is $78,000 a year, plus the $48,000 migration fee in the first renewal year.

# Memo — AI Vendor Proposal: Warranty Claim Coding and Service Message Triage

**To:** Dana Whitfield, Chief Financial Officer
**Re:** Go/no-go on the proposed platform
**Recommendation:** Conditional go — warranty claims first; messaging expands only after the pilot clears two conditions named below.

## 1. Fit

**Warranty claim coding fits well.** The work is high-volume (2,800 claims a month), rule-bound (match repair order lines to the manufacturer's labor codes and submit), and the current 4 percent first-pass denial rate already costs about $3,100 a month in rework and lost reimbursement. Document reading and coding is the vendor's mature product, and the reference customers' 55 to 65 percent savings figures are for exactly this use case.

**Message triage fits partially.** Sorting 9,200 messages a month by topic and urgency suits the platform. Drafting the replies does not, for two reasons visible in the appendix. Fourteen percent of messages involve open safety recalls or vehicle safety complaints, where a wrong or slow machine draft carries real liability. And 9 percent of messages arrive in Vietnamese, a language the classifier was never trained on, so roughly one message in eleven will be misrouted or left unread by the model. Messaging is the weaker case, and reply drafting should sit outside the pilot.

## 2. Return and payback

**Warranty claims.** 3.5 administrators at $58,000 is $203,000 a year. The vendor's promised 70 percent reduction is $142,100 a year. The reference range of 55 to 65 percent gives $111,650 to $131,950. Add denial reduction: if first-pass denials fall by half, the $37,200 annual rework and lost-reimbursement cost falls by about $18,600.

**Messages.** Six agents at $52,000 is $312,000; 55 percent of that is triage, or $171,600. The vendor's promised 60 percent reduction is $102,960. Applying the same haircut the reference customers show on claims (about 0.85 of the promise) gives roughly $87,500, and because the Vietnamese share gets no benefit, about $79,600.

**Cost.** $6,500 a month is $78,000 a year, plus the one-time $48,000 implementation in year one.

**Vendor scenario, both use cases:** $142,100 + $18,600 + $102,960 = $263,660 against $78,000; net annual benefit $185,660; payback on the $48,000 implementation in about three months.

**Reference scenario, both use cases:** $111,650 + $18,600 + $79,600 = $209,850; net annual benefit $131,850; payback in about four and a half months.

**Claims only, reference scenario:** $130,250 against $78,000; net $52,250; payback in about eleven months.

The result is most sensitive to the claim time-savings percentage. Every five points below 55 percent removes roughly $10,000 of annual benefit; at 30 percent savings the claims case alone no longer covers the subscription.

## 3. Risks and controls

Blocking before signature:
- **Customer personal and payment data leaving our systems.** Control: the data-processing agreement must specify US hosting, prohibit training on our data, and require deletion at termination. Owner: CFO with outside counsel.
- **Machine-drafted replies on recall and safety matters.** Control: reply drafting contractually disabled for the recall and safety-complaint categories, not merely switched off in settings. Owner: service operations director.

Managed after signature:
- **Vietnamese messages misclassified.** Control: any message the classifier scores under 70 percent confidence, or detects as a language other than English or Spanish, routes to a human queue; report the Vietnamese misroute rate monthly. Owner: service operations director.
- **Warranty coding errors.** Control: human approval stays on every claim above $2,000 and on any code match below 90 percent confidence; audit 50 auto-coded claims a week. Owner: warranty administration supervisor.
- **Model wrong in ways nobody notices.** Control: monthly reconciliation of model decisions against outcomes — denial rates by store and customer complaints about routing. Owner: group financial analyst.
- **Three-year lock-in.** Control: negotiate a twelve-month exit if the pilot thresholds are missed. Owner: CFO.

## 4. Rollout plan

**Pilot scope:** warranty claim coding at the four highest-volume stores, roughly 1,100 claims a month, plus message classification with no drafting at two of those stores.

**Duration:** ninety days after implementation.

**Success metrics:** handling time per claim (target under 5 minutes, from 11); first-pass denial rate (target under 2 percent, from 4); first-response time on messages in the pilot stores (target under 8 hours, from 19); Vietnamese misroute rate (target under 5 percent).

**Stopping rule:** if claim time savings are below 40 percent at day 60, halt the rollout and invoke the exit clause. Forty percent is the point at which the claims case alone slips to roughly a two-year payback.

## 5. Recommendation

Conditional go. Sign for warranty claim coding with both blocking controls written into the contract and the twelve-month exit in place. Run message classification in the pilot without drafting. Extend messaging to all eleven stores only if the Vietnamese misroute rate is under 5 percent and first-response time is under 8 hours at day 90. Do not enable machine-drafted replies on recall or safety complaints under any scenario.

MEMO TO: Chief Operating Officer
FROM: AP/Service Desk Analyst
RE: AI Platform Renewal Decision

1. Fit of Use Cases
Invoice reading/matching is a strong fit: invoices are structured documents with repeatable fields, and year-one results (42% time cut) already beat a break-even case even though they missed the 70% promise. Message triage is a weaker, conditional fit. The classifier only covers English/Spanish, but 8% of our 11,000 monthly messages (≈880) are Vietnamese and will be mishandled or silently dropped. Worse, 15% of messages (≈1,650/month) are habitability emergencies or legal/eviction notices — exactly the category where an unsupervised machine-drafted reply is highest-risk. Triage fits only with human sign-off gates on those categories.

2. Return and Payback
Current AP cost: 4 clerks × $60,000 = $240,000/yr. Service desk: 7 staff × $54,000 = $378,000/yr, half on triage = $189,000/yr baseline triage cost.

At vendor-promised rates (70% AP, 60% triage):
AP savings = $240,000 × 0.70 = $168,000/yr
Triage savings = $189,000 × 0.60 = $113,400/yr
Plus error-cost reduction ~$3,600/mo × 12 = $43,200/yr (assume proportional to AP time cut, ~70%=$30,240)
Total ≈ $311,640/yr. Annual cost = $86,400 (12×$7,200) + $36,000 upgrade (year 1) = $122,400.
Payback = $122,400 ÷ $311,640 ≈ 4.7 months.

At reference-customer range for AP (use 50%, keep measured 35% triage, since only AP has outside evidence):
AP savings = $240,000 × 0.50 = $120,000
Triage savings = $189,000 × 0.35 = $66,150
Error savings scaled at 50% = $21,600
Total ≈ $207,750/yr. Payback = $122,400 ÷ $207,750 ≈ 7.1 months.

The answer turns most on the triage percentage: AP savings hold up reasonably under both scenarios, but triage performance already missed target by 25 points in year one and is the input most exposed to language-coverage failure.

3. Risks and Controls
- Resident PII exposure: Control — DPA already signed, add quarterly access-log audit; Owner: IT Security Lead.
- Machine replies on emergencies/legal notices: Control — mandatory human review before send for the 15% flagged category; Owner: Service Desk Supervisor.
- Vietnamese coverage gap: Control — auto-route non-English/Spanish messages to human queue, track volume; Owner: Service Desk Supervisor.
- Model simply wrong: Control — weekly sampling audit of 50 AP matches and 50 replies, error log with clerk override; Owner: AP Manager.

4. Rollout Plan
Pilot covers AP only for 90 days at full volume; triage stays in shadow mode (drafts only, no auto-send) for the same period. Success metric: AP time reduction ≥50% and error rate ≤5%. Stopping rule: if triage shadow-mode accuracy on the 15% high-risk category falls below 90% agreement with staff-approved responses, or Vietnamese messages misroute above 2%, we halt full triage automation.

5. Recommendation
Renew on conditions: full go-live for AP; triage remains supervised/shadow until stopping-rule metrics are met, with contract renegotiated to tie fees to AP performance given triage's unresolved language and risk gaps.
